rule CobaltStrike_Beacon_HTTPS_C2 {
    meta:
        description = "Detects Cobalt Strike beaconing over HTTPS with common JA3 fingerprints"
        author = "SOC Team"
        reference = "https://attack.mitre.org/software/S0154/"
        date = "2026-04-09"
        tlp = "amber"
    strings:
        $ja3_fingerprint = "e4:9e:5b:4f:1c:8c:4b:4f:5f:7d:5f:4f:4f:4f:4f" // Common Cobalt Strike JA3
        $user_agent = "Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 6.1; WOW64; Trident/7.0; rv:11.0) like Gecko" wide ascii
        $uri_path = "/admin.php" wide ascii
    condition:
        ssl.ja3_hash == $ja3_fingerprint or
        (http.user_agent == $user_agent and http.uri == $uri_path)
}

arguments.summary: A low-severity port scan alert escalated to a critical enterprise-wide incident involving a nation-state adversary. Initial access was achieved via a phishing campaign targeting a finance user (jsmith@corp.local) on host WS-FIN-042 (10.0.5.42). Execution occurred through an encoded PowerShell command launched from Outlook, leading to the deployment of a Cobalt Strike beacon (rundll32.exe loading unsigned DLL from Temp). The threat actor established C2 communication with 198.51.100.23:443 and performed lateral movement using EternalBlue and ZeroLogon, compromising 20 additional critical assets including domain controllers, database servers, and email infrastructure. Immediate containment actions included blocking the source IP 10.0.5.14 at the firewall and conducting a full EPP scan on the initial host, which detected a Linux-specific dropper (likely a false positive or unrelated artifact). The scope of compromise is extensive, requiring full incident response, eradication, and recovery procedures.

arguments.summary: A low-severity port scan alert escalated to a critical enterprise-wide incident involving a coordinated nation-state campaign. The initial alert from IP 10.0.5.14 (host WS-FIN-042) was the reconnaissance phase of a Cobalt Strike-driven attack chain. Phishing via Outlook led to execution of an encoded PowerShell payload, which deployed a malicious DLL ('beacon.dll') via rundll32. The payload established C2 communication with 198.51.100.23 over HTTPS, performed host file modification, and initiated lateral movement via SMB and exploitation of EternalBlue and ZeroLogon vulnerabilities. SIEM correlation confirmed 20 additional hosts compromised across IT, Finance, Web, DB, and Domain Controller tiers. Active command and control, data collection (keylogging), and persistence mechanisms were identified. Immediate containment and eradication required.

    meta:
        description = "Detects dynamically generated Cobalt Strike beacons via C2 artifacts"
        author = "SOC Team"
        reference = "MITRE ATT&CK T1071.001"
        date = "2026-04-09"
    strings:
        $beacon_config = { 24 00 [1-100] 68 74 74 70 73?:// [a-zA-Z0-9./\\\\-_:]+ } // HTTPS C2 URL pattern
        $mutex_pattern = "Global\\\\MSCTF.Asm.{" 
        $reg_persistence = "HKCU\\\\Software\\\\Microsoft\\\\Windows\\\\CurrentVersion\\\\Run\\\\SysUpdate"
    condition:
        all of them
}
